2025-12.intuition: Forward elimination is already done, but back substitution still forms triangular sums of decreasing lengths.

2025-13.intuition: If every row of A sums to 1, the all-ones vector is an eigenvector with eigenvalue 1.

2025-22.intuition: For a missed positive sample, the update adds that sample and +1 bias, increasing its own score.

2025-24.intuition: Sums, differences, products, and quotients with nonzero denominator preserve differentiability.

2025-25.title: Orthonormal Sets and Bases
2025-25.intuition: R^n has infinitely many rotated orthonormal bases, and orthonormality is stronger than linear independence.

steps.heading: Basis uniqueness
steps.body: The standard basis is one orthonormal basis, but any orthogonal rotation supplies another; B is true and A false.

steps.heading: Implication
steps.body: An orthonormal set has zero inner products and unit norms, which forces linear independence. D is true; independent vectors need not be orthogonal, so C is false.

2025-26.title: Exact and Approximate Bayesian Inference
2025-26.intuition: Variable elimination is exact; Gibbs and rejection sampling are Monte Carlo approximations.

steps.body: It algebraically sums out hidden variables to compute exact conditional probabilities, so C is true and A false.

2025-27.title: When Binary Search Is Logarithmic
2025-27.intuition: Binary search needs both ordering and O(1) access to the middle element.

steps.body: Unsorted inputs A and B cannot discard half based on a comparison.

2025-28.intuition: For unit x, xx^T has eigenvalue 1 along x and 0 on the orthogonal complement.

2025-29.title: Exactly Two Insertion-sort Swaps
2025-29.intuition: Insertion sort's adjacent swap count equals the number of inversions in the original array.

steps.heading: Test x

2025-30.title: Single versus Complete Linkage
2025-30.intuition: Single linkage uses the closest cross-cluster pair; complete linkage uses the farthest.

2025-31.intuition: Weight each box's white-ball probability by its box-selection prior.
2025-31.shortcut: Create three prior x likelihood weights, then normalize the requested one.

2025-32.title: Rationalizing a Radical Limit
2025-32.intuition: The two large terms cancel, so rationalize to expose the small difference.

steps.body: sqrt(t^2+t)-t = t/(sqrt(t^2+t)+t).

2025-33.intuition: Compute the inner maximum first, then count all outer rows above it.

2025-36.title: Variance of a Squared Standard Normal
2025-36.intuition: Z=(X-mu)/sigma is standard normal, so Y=Z^2 follows chi-square with one degree of freedom.

steps.heading: Identify the distribution
steps.body: Z~N(0,1), hence Y=Z^2~chi-square(1).

steps.heading: Use its variance
steps.body: A chi-square variable with k degrees of freedom has variance 2k, giving 2.

2025-37.title: Rank under A cubed equals A
2025-37.intuition: A^3=A implies A=A*A^2 and A^2=A^3*A? The clean route is comparing kernels.

steps.heading: Compare kernels
steps.body: If Ax=0 then A^2x=0. Conversely, if A^2x=0, then Ax=A^3x=A(A^2x)=0.

steps.heading: Use rank-nullity
steps.body: Null(A)=Null(A^2), so their nullities and therefore ranks are equal.

2025-38.title: Gram Matrix of Independent Vectors
2025-38.intuition: A is the Gram matrix X^T X of independent columns, so every nonzero quadratic form is a squared norm.

steps.heading: Write the quadratic form
steps.body: For z not zero, z^T A z = ||sum_i z_i x_i||^2.

steps.body: M^5=I because five rotations total 2pi. Since 2026 mod 5=1, M^2026=M.

2026-21.shortcut: Reduce the exponent modulo the rotation period.

2026-22.title: Ball Intersected with a Plane Subspace
2026-22.intuition: S1 is the radius-4 closed ball centered at the origin. A two-dimensional subspace is a plane through the origin.

steps.heading: Intersect
steps.body: The plane cuts the ball in a disk of radius 4.

steps.heading: Area
steps.body: pi r^2=pi*16=16pi.

2026-22.shortcut: Central plane section of a radius-r ball is a radius-r disk.
mistakes: Using sphere surface area instead of disk area.

2026-23.title: Matching ML Tasks to Algorithms
2026-23.intuition: Match each algorithm by its standard purpose.

steps.heading: Map
steps.body: Clustering->K-Medoid; Classification->Naive Bayes; Sampling->MCMC; Feature extraction->LDA.

steps.heading: Select
steps.body: This is exactly option B.

2026-24.title: Logical Entailment
2026-24.intuition: X entails Y means there is no interpretation where X is true and Y false.

steps.heading: Equivalent forms
steps.body: Therefore X->Y is valid, 'if X then Y' says the same, and X AND not-Y is unsatisfiable/false.

steps.heading: Reject converse
steps.body: Y->X need not follow.

mistakes: Assuming entailment is symmetric.

cheat.rule: X implies Y; X and not-Y impossible

2026-25.title: Reconstructing a Binary Tree
2026-25.intuition: Preorder gives each subtree root; inorder splits its left and right members.

steps.heading: Build
steps.body: P is root. Left inorder S,Q,E with preorder Q,S,E gives Q children S,E. Right inorder F,R,G with preorder R,F,G gives R children F,G.

steps.heading: Check options
steps.body: Postorder is S,E,Q,F,G,R,P. Thus A and B are true; Q has two children and G lies in R's right subtree.

2026-25.shortcut: Root from preorder, split by its position in inorder, recurse.
mistakes: Reading preorder as root-left-right without using inorder boundaries.

2026-26.title: Operations Safe for a Foreign Key
2026-26.intuition: Adding a parent or deleting a child cannot create an orphan reference.

steps.heading: Safe operations
steps.body: Inserting into r adds a referenced parent; deleting from s removes referencing children. Both never violate the FK.

steps.heading: Risky operations
steps.body: Deleting a referenced r row or inserting an s row with nonexistent E may violate it.

2026-26.shortcut: Parent insert and child delete are always safe.
mistakes: Assuming child insert is safe without checking parent existence.

cheat.trap: Direction is child E -> parent A

2026-27.title: Roots and Extrema of a Cubic
2026-27.intuition: Factor f and classify stationary points on the restricted domain.

steps.heading: Roots
steps.body: f(x)=x^3-3x^2+2=(x-1)(x^2-2x-2), so x=1 is a root; only one root lies near [-0.9,0], not two.

steps.heading: Extrema
steps.body: f'=3x(x-2). Sign changes show a local maximum at 0 and minimum at 2. On (-1,3], these are the only such extrema.

2026-27.shortcut: Factor after spotting x=1, then use f' sign chart.
mistakes: Counting the excluded endpoint -1 as an attained extremum.

cheat.rule: Roots by factorization; extrema by derivative plus endpoints

2026-28.title: Normal versus t1 Distribution
2026-28.intuition: Both distributions are symmetric about zero, but t1 is lower at the center and heavier in the tails.

steps.heading: At zero
steps.body: Symmetry gives G(0)=H(0)=0.5, so A true; their densities at zero differ, so D false.

steps.heading: At crossing c
steps.body: Before positive density crossing, the normal accumulates more central mass, leaving G(c)>H(c); by symmetry G(-c)<H(-c). Thus C true and B false.

2026-28.shortcut: Student-t has heavier tails and less central concentration than normal.
mistakes: Confusing density equality at c with CDF equality at c.

cheat.rule: Same median; t has more tail probability

2026-29.title: One SGD Update
2026-29.intuition: Differentiate the objective f_w(x)=wx with respect to w.

steps.heading: Gradient
steps.body: df/dw=x=10.

2026-29.shortcut: SGD subtracts learning-rate times current-sample gradient.
mistakes: Differentiating with respect to x instead of w.

2026-30.title: Minimax Root Strategy
2026-30.intuition: MIN chooses the smallest terminal value below each root action; MAX then chooses the largest of those minima.

steps.heading: Back up MIN nodes
steps.body: Take the minimum of the three displayed leaf utilities for each of MAX's strategies 1,2,3.

steps.heading: Choose at root
steps.body: The largest backed-up value occurs under strategy 2.

mistakes: Letting MAX choose the largest leaf directly while ignoring MIN's reply.

2026-31.title: Failed Binary Search Comparisons
2026-31.intuition: Each unsuccessful comparison roughly halves the remaining 1000 positions until the interval is empty.

steps.heading: Conclude
steps.body: In the worst case, 10 middle-element comparisons are required before absence is established.

2026-32.intuition: A non-leaf node with p pointers stores p-1 search keys.

2026-33.intuition: f(f(n))=n means every permutation cycle has length 1 or 2.

2026-35.shortcut: Independent rectangular double sum factors into two sums.

2026-36.title: First HAC Merge by Manhattan Distance
2026-36.intuition: At the first agglomerative step every cluster is a singleton, so compare all point-pair distances.

2026-37.title: Ridge Regression Bias-variance Tradeoff
2026-37.intuition: Ridge shrinks coefficients to reduce sensitivity to training noise.

steps.body: Ridge uses an L2 penalty, not L1.

steps.heading: Effect
steps.body: Shrinkage can increase bias but generally reduces prediction variance and overfitting.

2026-38.intuition: The rule applies only to creative people: within C, success is equivalent to discipline.

steps.heading: Reject others

2026-39.title: Counting Recursive Activations
2026-39.intuition: Count calls, including base cases, with C(n)=1+C(n-1)+C(n-2).
2026-39.shortcut: Compute the call-count recurrence, not the returned numeric value.

2026-40.title: Reachability after Reversing Edges
2026-40.intuition: A path v->...->u in G reverses to u->...->v in G^R.

steps.heading: Use path reversal
steps.body: If DFS in G from v reaches u, a directed v-to-u path exists.

steps.heading: Reverse
steps.body: In G^R that path runs from u to v, so BFS from u reaches v. Traversal method changes order, not reachability.

2026-40.shortcut: Reverse graph swaps the direction of every reachability relation.
mistakes: Assuming BFS and DFS from the same start visit paths in reverse order.

2026-41.title: B+ Tree Leaf Split Propagation
2026-41.intuition: Insert 3 into its sorted leaf; overflow splits the leaf and may update parent separators, but root capacity determines whether the root itself splits.

steps.heading: Insert and split
steps.body: The target leaf exceeds two keys, so divide it and promote/copy the new right leaf's first key upward.

steps.heading: Update root
steps.body: Following the shown tree's parent split, the resulting root stores only separator 5.

2026-41.shortcut: Leaf split copies up the first key of the new right leaf.
mistakes: Removing the promoted key from a B+ leaf as in a B-tree.

2026-42.title: Natural-join Expression Evaluation
2026-42.intuition: Natural joins require equality on every common attribute, so evaluate each bracket with its selections before the final join.

steps.heading: Left and right intermediates
steps.body: X natural-join Y matches common P,Q; apply Q=Q3 OR R=R2. Separately Y natural-join Z matches P and keep S>1.

steps.heading: Final join
steps.body: The surviving intermediates have no mutually matching common-attribute combination, so projection PRS returns zero rows.

2026-42.shortcut: Write intermediate tuples; do not reason only from individual P values.
mistakes: Joining on P alone when Q is also common to X and Y.

cheat.trap: Apply selections at the stated level

2026-43.title: Counting Data Cuboids from Hierarchies
2026-43.intuition: For independent dimensions, choose one aggregation level from each hierarchy, including ALL where shown.

steps.heading: Count levels
steps.body: Read the usable level counts from each displayed concept hierarchy.

steps.heading: Multiply
steps.body: The product of those choices is 4^3=64, represented in the options as 4^3.

2026-43.shortcut: Cuboids equal the product of level-choice counts across dimensions.
mistakes: Adding hierarchy levels instead of multiplying independent choices.

2026-44.title: Variance after a Random Sign Multiplier
2026-44.intuition: 2X-1 is either -1 or +1, so multiplying Y only flips its sign.

steps.heading: Mean
steps.body: Independence and E[Y]=0 give E[(2X-1)Y]=0.

steps.heading: Second moment
steps.body: (2X-1)^2=1 always, so variance=E[Y^2]=Var(Y)=100.

2026-44.shortcut: An independent random sign does not change a zero-mean variable's variance.
mistakes: Using Var(2X-1)*Var(Y), which is not a general product-variance rule.

2026-45.title: Poisson Probability at Its Mean
2026-45.intuition: The sum is P(Poisson(n)<=n). A Poisson(n) variable centered at its mean becomes asymptotically normal.

steps.heading: Recognize CDF
steps.body: e^-n sum(k=0 to n) n^k/k! is P(X_n<=n) for X_n~Poisson(n).

steps.heading: Take limit
steps.body: After standardization, the cutoff is at zero; the normal CDF at zero is 0.5.

2026-45.shortcut: Large Poisson is approximately Normal(mean n, variance n).
mistakes: Treating the partial exponential sum as the full e^n series.

2026-46.title: Trace of a Rotation Block
2026-46.intuition: The sum of eigenvalues is the trace, avoiding explicit characteristic-polynomial work.

steps.heading: Write trace
steps.body: gamma1+gamma2+gamma3=1+2 cos t.

steps.heading: Solve
steps.body: Set 1+2cos t=1+sqrt2, so cos t=1/sqrt2. On [-pi,pi], t=pi/4 or -pi/4.

mistakes: Solving sin t=1/sqrt2 from off-diagonal entries.

cheat.trap: List all solutions in the interval

2026-47.title: Confusion-matrix Metrics
2026-47.intuition: Build counts: actual X=20 gives 14 predicted X and 6 predicted Y; actual Y=10 gives 2 predicted X and 8 predicted Y.

steps.heading: Accuracy
steps.body: Correct=14+8=22 of 30, so accuracy=11/15.

steps.heading: Precisions and recalls
steps.body: Precision X=14/(14+2)=14/16; precision Y=8/(8+6)=8/14, so X is higher. Recall X=14/20=0.7; recall Y=8/10=0.8, so C false.

2026-47.shortcut: Write the 2x2 table before applying any metric.
mistakes: Confusing precision with recall denominators.

cheat.rule: Precision uses predicted column; recall uses actual row

2026-48.title: Valid Quantifier Implications
2026-48.intuition: On a nonempty domain, a universal claim implies an existential instance, but one witness never proves universality.

steps.heading: Check A
steps.body: If P holds for every x, it holds for some x, so A is valid.

steps.heading: Reject B,C,D
steps.body: Existence does not imply all; hence the biconditional also fails. If all have P, it cannot imply that some lacks P.

2026-48.shortcut: Use a two-element counterexample for existential-to-universal claims.
mistakes: Treating forall and exists as interchangeable.

cheat.rule: Universal implies existential only for nonempty domains

2026-49.title: Bubble versus Insertion Sort on a Nearly Sorted Array
2026-49.intuition: Only 5 and 4 form an inversion, so insertion sort needs one swap; both algorithms still inspect already ordered pairs.

steps.heading: Insertion sort
steps.body: The first three insertions make routine comparisons; inserting 4 swaps once with 5, so N2 is small and exactly one swap occurs.

steps.heading: Bubble sort
steps.body: Standard bubble sort makes more comparisons than insertion sort here and performs unnecessary comparisons too. Thus B,C,D hold; A's exact N2=4 is not correct for the stated counting convention.

2026-49.shortcut: Inversion count gives adjacent swaps, not necessarily comparisons.
mistakes: Equating one inversion with one total comparison.

cheat.trap: Comparison count depends on loop tests

2026-50.title: Independent Python Closures
2026-50.intuition: Each call to outer creates a new private list captured by its returned inner function.

steps.heading: Trace f1
steps.body: f1 calls produce [10], then [10,20], then [10,20,40].

steps.heading: Trace f2
steps.body: f2 has a different x, so its first call produces [30]. Thus B and D are correct.

2026-50.shortcut: One outer invocation equals one closure state.
mistakes: Treating captured x like the shared mutable default-argument case.

cheat.rule: Each factory call captures a fresh environment
cheat.trap: Calls through the same closure share state

2026-51.title: SQL Team Size per Employee
2026-51.intuition: First compute one count per TeamID, then join that result back to each employee.

steps.heading: Evaluate A
steps.body: Its subquery groups by TeamID and returns TeamID,count; joining on E.TeamID correctly assigns each employee the team count.

steps.heading: Reject others
steps.body: B additionally equates EmpID, reducing count to one. C groups by employee. D's subquery omits TeamID but later references it, so it is invalid.

2026-52.title: Centering Projection Matrix
2026-52.intuition: M=I-(1/n)11^T removes the component along the all-ones direction.

steps.heading: Symmetry
steps.body: Both I and 11^T are symmetric, so M^T=M.

steps.heading: Idempotence
steps.body: Using 1^T1=n, expand M^2=I-(2/n)11^T+(1/n^2)1(n)1^T=M. Hence it is a projection. Its trace is n-1, not n.

mistakes: Claiming M^2=I; projection means M^2=M.

cheat.rule: Orthogonal projector onto vectors with zero sum

2026-53.title: Chi-square Facts for Normal Samples
2026-53.intuition: Sums of squares of independent standard normals are chi-square; centering consumes one degree of freedom.

steps.heading: A and B
steps.body: sum X_i^2~chi-square(n). Also sum(X_i-Xbar)^2~chi-square(n-1).

steps.heading: C and D
steps.body: X1^2+Xn^2~chi-square(2), which is Exponential with mean 2, so C true. sqrt(n)Xbar is one standard normal; its square is chi-square(1), not 2.

2026-53.shortcut: Each independent squared standard normal contributes one degree of freedom.
mistakes: Forgetting the one df lost by estimating the sample mean.

cheat.rule: Chi-square df equals independent squared components

2026-54.title: CDF Properties for a Discrete Variable
2026-54.intuition: A CDF accumulates probability, so it is nondecreasing and jumps at mass points.

steps.heading: Check statements
steps.body: F may equal zero, so it is not always strictly positive. It is nondecreasing and a nondegenerate discrete distribution has jump discontinuities. CDFs are right-continuous, not left-continuous.

mistakes: Calling a CDF left-continuous.

2026-55.intuition: Compute prediction and absolute error, then add 0.20 times the squared L2 norm.
mistakes: Using 0.20||w||=1 instead of 0.20||w||^2=5.

2026-56.title: MLP Parameter Count without Biases
2026-56.intuition: Each pair of adjacent fully connected layers contributes input-size times output-size weights.

steps.heading: Add

2026-57.title: Disease Probability after a Positive Test
2026-57.intuition: Compare true-positive mass with all positive-test mass.
2026-57.shortcut: Imagine 100 people: 24 true positives and 7 false positives.

2026-58.title: Repeated Bubble Pass Swap Count
2026-58.intuition: fun performs one left-to-right bubble pass and returns its swaps; repeated passes sort the list.

steps.heading: Connect to inversions
steps.body: Every adjacent out-of-order swap reduces the inversion count by exactly one, and the repeated passes eventually remove all inversions.

2026-59.intuition: The z clause is automatically satisfied by choosing z=t; the real filter is whether Y has a same-P row with S>1.

2026-60.intuition: For each account compare how many balances are higher versus lower.

2026-61.title: ER-to-relational Mapping Count
2026-61.intuition: Each strong entity gets a relation, a multivalued attribute gets its own relation, and an M:N relationship gets a bridge relation.

steps.body: E1 relation + E2 relation + separate relation for E2's multivalued A22 + relation for R12 =4.

2026-62.title: Pairwise Squared Distances and Variance
2026-62.intuition: The double sum of pairwise squared distances equals 2n times the sum of squared deviations from the mean.

steps.heading: Use identity
steps.body: sum_i sum_j (x_i-x_j)^2=2n sum_i (x_i-xbar)^2.

steps.heading: Substitute the stated scaling
steps.body: With n=100 and the given normalized pairwise value 2000/99, rearrangement yields (1/99)sum_i(x_i-xbar)^2=10.

mistakes: Forgetting the double sum counts both (i,j) and (j,i).

2026-63.title: Zero Correlation by Symmetry
2026-63.intuition: Given X=x, Y is centered at x^2, an even function of x; symmetric X makes its linear covariance vanish.

steps.heading: Covariance
steps.body: E[XY]=E[X*E(Y|X)]=E[X^3]=0 by symmetry on [-1,1]. Also E[X]=0, so Cov(X,Y)=0 and correlation=0.

2026-63.shortcut: Odd moments of a symmetric zero-centered distribution vanish.
mistakes: Assuming dependence always implies nonzero correlation.

2026-64.title: Overlapping Row-sum and Column-sum Events
2026-64.intuition: The second row and third column share one Bernoulli cell; condition on that cell.

steps.heading: Shared cell=1
steps.body: Then the other four cells in each line must contain exactly 2 ones: probability 0.5*[C(4,2)/16]^2.

steps.heading: Shared cell=0
steps.body: Then each group of four needs exactly 3 ones: probability 0.5*[C(4,3)/16]^2. Sum=0.5*(36+16)/256=26/256=0.1015625.

2026-64.shortcut: Condition on the single intersection cell to make the remaining groups independent.
mistakes: Multiplying two Binomial(5,0.5) probabilities as if row and column were independent.

cheat.trigger: Row and column sums share one cell

2026-65.title: Maximum Rayleigh Quotient of the Centering Matrix
2026-65.intuition: A=I-(1/n)11^T is an orthogonal projection with eigenvalues 1 on the zero-sum subspace and 0 along 1.

steps.heading: Use Rayleigh quotient
steps.body: For unit x, x^T A x is at most the largest eigenvalue of symmetric A.

steps.heading: Maximize
steps.body: lambda_max(A)=1, attained by any unit vector orthogonal to 1. Therefore the maximum is 1.

2026-65.shortcut: Maximum unit Rayleigh quotient equals largest eigenvalue.
mistakes: Using trace n-1 as the maximum value.

cheat.trap: Trace sums eigenvalues; it is not the maximum
